Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

fastglm 0.1.3

Bug fixes

  • fastglm_ordinal() now stops when named count-matrix columns do not match levels in order, as fastglm_ordinal_streaming() already did. These columns were previously assigned by position, which could silently reverse a fit.
  • Printed coefficient tables without p-values no longer round small estimates, standard errors, or bootstrap limits to zero.
  • Streamed GLM, negative-binomial, hurdle, two-part, and ordinal fits no longer retain the last source block, so saving a fit does not write those rows.
  • predict(type="class") for ordinal source fits no longer depends on the factor method for c(), which requires R 4.1.0.
  • Models without a size parameter no longer print a missing Theta row.

Performance

  • Common-slope ordinal maximum likelihood now begins with observed-information Newton steps, whose cost does not grow with the number of categories. Expected information still certifies convergence and gives the reported covariance, and estimates and standard errors are unchanged within the convergence tolerance. Streamed fits read their source fewer times. control=list(observed=FALSE) restores expected scoring throughout.
  • Ordinal design setup, category totals, and block scaling now run in C++, and probit kernels compute both tails together.
  • Ordinal fits with many categories now use a block factorization and structured coordinate changes instead of dense matrix products. information.rcond now reports the exact one-norm value rather than an estimate.
  • Negative-binomial, hurdle, and truncated-count block calculations for dense designs now run in C++, and dense matrix fits no longer copy or revalidate rows on each pass. Streamed GLM validation allocates less.
  • Threshold-specific ordinal maximum likelihood also begins with observed-information Newton steps.
  • Threshold-specific maximum-likelihood fits that reach the ordering boundary now stop with convergence.reason = "ordering_boundary" and a message explaining the cause, instead of using every remaining iteration.
  • Ordinal common-slope score moments and logit and probit sandwich blocks now run in C++, reusing the fitting kernels.
  • Constrained ordinal iterations for profile intervals and likelihood-ratio and score tests now run in C++, with results that match the earlier R loop.

Model interfaces and inference

  • Ordinal source fits now support prediction scores and cumulative calibration directly through fastglm_ordinal_assess(). The default retains compact summaries; keep.rows collects row scores and sink writes them blockwise. Dense and streamed assessments use the same frequency and loss conventions.

  • Common-slope tests now operate directly on ordinal sources, including complete terms, separate partial-model term nulls, ordinary score tests with ML or reduced-null meanBR estimation, and partial-model ML likelihood ratios. Refits and information calculations retain bounded observation-block storage.

  • Added optional ordinal boundary-row diagnostics through fastglm_diagnostics(boundary=TRUE). Tables identify the smallest category probabilities and predictor gaps, observed frequencies, and source rows. Raw and standardized scores are labeled by their parameter coordinates. These diagnostics do not certify absence of an interior solution.

  • Partial ordinal evaluation computes each compensated adjacent predictor gap once and limits logit-specific gap calculations to the logit link. The probability equations, arithmetic order, and convergence criteria are retained.

  • Added a sufficient preflight check for saturated, fully varying logit models with mean bias reduction. An absent intermediate category within a predictor pattern can force a boundary solution despite all categories being observed overall. Certified cases now explain the unavailable interior solution before iteration; other boundary failures retain their existing diagnostics.

  • Partial ordinal fitting reuses the predictor-step bound already calculated for its first scoring direction. This removes a duplicate source scan while preserving direction scaling, probability ordering, and fallback checks.

  • Extended fastglm_po_test() to partial ordinal models. Complete terms can be tested for common slopes while other varying effects remain unrestricted, with joint or term-specific score tests and an ML likelihood-ratio option. The meanBR null option retains its ordinary projected-score convention; full-model adjusted-score hypotheses remain available through fastglm_score_test().

  • Added HC0/HC1 and clustered covariance for streamed common-slope and partial ordinal fits. One source pass accumulates the same observed-information and ordinary-score contributions as dense fits. Cluster labels are matched across blocks without rounding numeric identifiers, and storage depends on the block, coefficient dimension, and number of clusters.

  • Added selected threshold-specific effects through nonparallel in dense, prepared, and streamed ordinal fits. Partial proportional odds and nonparallel probit and complementary log-log models support maximum likelihood and full-model mean bias reduction, formula terms or matrix column selections, grouped frequencies, and offsets. Training and prediction checks enforce valid cumulative probabilities at the relevant predictor values.

  • Added readable partial-model summaries, full expected-information covariance, Wald intervals and term tests, probability standard errors, averages, and prediction assessment. The ordinal vignette explains the model, prediction domain, and bias-reduced wine example. Retained partial fits also support robust and clustered covariance, automatic marginal effects, ML profiles, and ordinary or full-model adjusted-score tests. Linear profile contrasts can test equality of selected varying slopes while other effects remain unrestricted. Partial models still require every declared category to have positive frequency; refitting bootstrap support remains limited to common slopes.

  • Corrected cumulative Pearson residuals for ordinal probit and complementary log-log fits to use the binomial variance of each cumulative indicator.

  • Added ML profile-likelihood intervals and joint likelihood-ratio tests for retained dense ordinal fits, and fastglm_score_test() for ordinary or full-model mean-bias-adjusted ordinal scores under linear constraints. The procedures use first-order chi-square references, retain constrained-fit diagnostics, and require every category to be observed. Profile intervals have a compact shared display; failed limits remain missing.

  • Added fastglm_ordinal_streaming() for repeatable sources, with logit, probit, and complementary log-log links, maximum likelihood and mean bias reduction, frequency counts, and offsets. Category and rank checks combine all blocks. The bias adjustment uses information from the complete source. Predictions, residuals, and weights support block destinations without collecting the complete result. Model-based covariance is retained; robust covariance rereads the source, while constrained coefficient inference requires retained data.

  • Reduced binomial probit and complementary log-log post-fit overhead by combining accurate likelihood and residual summaries, reusing the solver’s current deviance, and calculating prediction derivatives without allocating unused probability summaries. The estimating equations are unchanged.

  • Binomial probit and complementary log-log bias reduction now evaluates tail probabilities, scores, and information without separately flooring means and derivatives. This corrects the estimating equations for nearly deterministic outcomes. QR and SVD adjustments avoid amplification of roundoff in rows with tiny working weights. Likelihoods, residuals, and diagnostics use the same calculations across dense, sparse, mapped, and streamed fits.

  • Logistic ordinal fitting reuses threshold-gap calculations and algebraic probability identities to reduce exponential and logarithm evaluations without storing observation-level probability arrays. Binary probit and complementary log-log bias reduction uses bounded Fisher scoring, retaining checks of the adjusted score and remaining predictor change.

  • Binomial probit and complementary log-log mean bias reduction now limits oversized scoring updates on the linear-predictor scale. Sparse, mapped, and streamed fits use current information for these adjustments, avoiding delayed adjustment oscillation. Diagnostics report reduced steps. Streaming null deviances handle all-zero/all-one binomial outcomes with offsets directly.

  • Extended fastglm_wald_test() to truncated, hurdle, zero-inflated, and two-part fits. Component selection, complete formula terms, and named contrasts retain joint regression covariance, including supplied cross-component covariance. Estimated negative-binomial size boundaries return unavailable tests.

  • Ordinal models now support probit and complementary log-log links with maximum likelihood and mean bias reduction. Predictions, marginal effects, expected and robust covariance, assessment, common-slope score tests, prepared designs, and bootstrap refits retain the selected link.

  • Dense Firth GLMs with a numerically zero-rank working design no longer report successful convergence from a zero coefficient update.

  • Added fastglm_wald_test() for joint formula-term tests and named linear coefficient contrasts in GLMs and ordinal models, with model-based or supplied covariance and the shared test display. Nonestimability and unavailable covariance remain explicit; the chi-square reference is a first-order approximation.

  • Proportional-odds score tests now use the tridiagonal threshold information directly, reducing intermediate allocations. fastglm_po_test(by.term=TRUE) shares one null fit and one information calculation across joint and term-specific tests, with readable tables and numeric extraction.

  • Unified printed model, summary, diagnostics, prediction, bootstrap, and hypothesis-test output with common headings, aligned tables, display precision, and fitting status. Test results retain numeric fields and provide as.data.frame() and optional broom::tidy() extraction, including failure explanations. Diagnostics use readable solver names and labeled numerical checks. Predictions with standard errors print aligned tables and support as.data.frame(), while retaining the original fit and se.fit components. Vignettes use these displays directly.

  • Added fastglm_po_test() for direct proportional-odds testing and an explicit null.estimation = "meanBR" option (po.estimation within assessment). This evaluates the ordinary nuisance-projected score at a bias-reduced null; its chi-square reference has first-order justification. A sufficient separation check identifies two-valued predictor groups observed only in an endpoint category. ML separation is reported before optimization; empty categories and deficient rank remain unsupported.

  • Added an optional analytic proportional-odds score test to fastglm_ordinal_assess(), using an ML null refit and expected Fisher information. Joint and selected-term tests support frequency counts and offsets. Empty categories, deficient designs, failed null fits, and unusable information return explicit diagnostics and unavailable p-values. The test uses a first-order chi-square reference without resampling.

  • Added fastglm_marginal_effects() for average derivatives of ordinal category and cumulative probabilities with respect to a continuous predictor. Formula interactions and smooth transformations are differentiated together, with offsets held fixed and delta-method uncertainty for thresholds and slopes.

  • Added ordinal prediction assessment with logarithmic and ranked probability scores, cumulative calibration plots, and descriptive threshold-specific slope comparisons. Frequency counts contribute individual-observation scores, and supplied evaluation outcomes are kept separate from fitting.

  • Ordinal parametric bootstraps now reuse response-independent design setup within each process while retaining replicate-specific fitting diagnostics.

  • Added fastglm_ordinal_prepare() and fastglm_ordinal_batch() for repeated ordinal responses on a common predictor design. Saved centering, scaling, and rank checks are reused when predictors and effective row frequencies agree; changed inputs rebuild the preparation. Formula metadata and ordinary R serialization are retained, with separate category mappings and convergence diagnostics for each fit.

  • Added ordinal simulation, probability-scale and cumulative residuals, and optional broom tidy, glance, and augment methods. Simulation preserves effective category frequencies without expanding grouped observations.

  • Added HC0/HC1 and cluster covariance for ordinal fits, using the observed ordinary-score Jacobian and explicit frequency semantics. For mean bias reduction this is a first-order sandwich convention, with regularity and positive-category requirements. Supplied covariance matrices can be used in summaries, tidy output, and average probability contrasts.

  • Added ordinal pairs, cluster, and parametric refitting bootstraps. Replicate diagnostics retain failures and category changes. Uncertainty summaries remain unavailable when refits fail or an interior category is empty. For mean bias-reduced parametric bootstraps, empty endpoints are allowed when all interior categories remain represented in the original fit and every refit.

  • Added cumulative-logit proportional-odds models through fastglm_ordinal(), with formula and matrix interfaces, maximum likelihood and mean bias reduction, frequency counts, offsets, and native fitting. Empty interior categories retain their labels through an explicit reduced model mapping; tied-threshold Wald uncertainty is unavailable. Category/cumulative predictions, model-based standard errors, and average probability contrasts use the common model interface.

  • Added method = "qr" to streaming GLMs, including mean bias reduction. Incremental QR avoids weighted crossproducts in initialization and fitting, retaining a triangular factor for covariance, prediction uncertainty, leverage, robust covariance, and average-prediction inference. Rank is assessed across the complete source; globally redundant columns still produce an explicit error. The default Cholesky solver is unchanged.

  • Added penalized profile-likelihood intervals through confint(..., method = "profile") and joint coefficient tests through fastglm_profile_test() for retained dense binomial-logit Firth fits. Constrained fits retain the full original Jeffreys penalty. The procedures support binomial counts and frequency weights, use an asymptotic chi-square reference, and report numerical failures through missing results and diagnostics.

  • Added firth to prepared designs and batch fits. Dense Gaussian-identity, Gamma-log, and Poisson-square-root batches reuse common setup with the automatic or LLT solver; other solvers retain their requested decomposition. Modified predictors or weights invalidate the saved setup, and prepared objects remain serializable across R sessions and process workers.

  • Extended estimated-theta negative-binomial, hurdle, and two-part fitting to sparse matrices and repeatable block readers, with consistent offsets, formula transformations, and joint theta uncertainty.

  • Added joint HC0/HC1 and cluster covariance for count and two-part models, average response contrasts, and refitting bootstrap uncertainty. Bootstrap output records failed fits, preserves reproducible replicate seeds, and supports sparse designs and repeatable sources.

  • Added a direct formula interface, named and automatic solver choices, prediction with offsets and term standard errors, leverage, simulation, Wald intervals, numerical diagnostics, and optional broom methods.

  • Added reusable designs and batch fitting, including a shared Gaussian factorization, optional process workers, and controls for retained data and inference. inference = "none" skips covariance calculation.

  • Added standalone zero-truncated Poisson/NB regression and two-part binomial/Gamma regression for nonnegative continuous outcomes.

  • Count models now provide component and marginal predictions, probability masses, delta-method standard errors, summaries, residuals, and simulation. Theta profile intervals are available for ordinary, truncated, and hurdle NB.

  • Added resettable sources with fixed formula schemas and optional DBI and Parquet adapters. Streaming fits support prediction and diagnostic sinks, robust/cluster covariance, and average predictions and contrasts.

Numerical corrections

  • Streaming QR Firth convergence now checks the actual remaining changes in fitted linear predictors, joint adjusted scores, and dispersion. The criterion avoids requiring tiny changes to large cancelling coefficients. Additional precision is used to verify highly ill-conditioned designs; fits that fail the verified criteria still report nonconvergence.

  • Safeguarded Gamma-log mean bias reduction against initial coefficient steps that overshoot the adjusted-score solution. Firth diagnostics now distinguish ordinary and adjusted coefficient scores, report the adjusted dispersion score where applicable, and retain the solver’s convergence reason. Source initialization uses consistent fitted means and derivatives for very small responses. Gamma-log null models with offsets use their explicit score solution, avoiding a separate unstable intercept-only iteration.

  • Stabilized negative-binomial theta scores and likelihood calculations near the Poisson limit. Boundary theta estimates have explicitly unavailable theta standard errors; SE.theta elsewhere uses joint observed information. The default beta-only NB covariance retains the usual expected-information convention, while vcov(..., full = TRUE) includes theta jointly.

  • Truncated NB means and likelihood now correspond to the returned coefficients and theta even when the outer iteration limit is reached.

  • Preserved sequential readers during component fits and bootstrap resampling, retained external source offsets in new-data prediction, and corrected simulation of numeric binomial proportions with integer trial weights.

  • Fixed rank-deficient QR updates and aliased coefficient reporting. Explicit Cholesky solves reject singular or ill-conditioned information matrices; automatic dense fits can fall back to pivoted QR. Calls that previously returned arbitrary coefficients or invalid covariance matrices can now fail explicitly. Callers with redundant predictors should use pivoted QR or method = "auto" and handle aliased coefficients as NA.

  • Unified matrix/formula initialization and model accounting, including grouped-binomial trials, zero-weight degrees of freedom, offset null models, fixed dispersion, NB AIC, and working residuals.

  • Native family dispatch preserves modified-family callback semantics and exact negative-binomial theta parameters.

  • Fixed mapped matrix views and matrix products involving row/column offsets.

  • Gamma mean bias reduction now solves the adjusted dispersion equation. Supported families and the distinction between adjusted scores and penalized likelihood are documented explicitly.

  • Hurdle NB covariance now uses joint coefficient–theta observed information. Truncated-count iterations check likelihood improvement, and small-rate derivatives use the correct limits. Component offsets are handled separately.

  • Information matrices are evaluated at the reported estimate. Indefinite mixture information no longer produces standard errors from absolute values.

  • Streaming validates every chunk, uses family-specific initialization, and propagates source errors. Grouped-binomial likelihoods retain trial totals.

Performance and verification

  • Added a reproducible ordinal uncertainty development study comparing model-based, sandwich, and bootstrap intervals across small samples, rare categories, correlated predictors, and independent clusters. Results retain unavailable intervals and failures separately from conditional coverage.

  • Added a reproducible ordinal development study spanning small samples, rare categories, separation, correlated predictors, grouped frequencies, and larger predictor/category dimensions. It distinguishes convergence, reduced-category fits, and regular interval coverage, with simulation error reported separately from computational performance.

  • Replaced numerical differentiation in joint count-model information with analytic derivatives, retaining coefficient–theta dependence, mixture cross-component terms, and the existing covariance validity checks.

  • Reused constant Firth information matrices in sparse, mapped, and callback fits. Gamma-log fitting also reuses the common adjustment after its initial calculation. Gamma callback fits combine repeated prior weights within each block while preserving sequential reads and bounded block storage.

  • Included NEWS.md in source packages so the README link resolves in the packaged source; this repairs the incoming-check note from Windows.

  • Accelerated Gamma mean bias reduction by combining identical prior weights in its dispersion equation and replacing fixed bisection with a safeguarded Brent solve. Constant-weight Firth fits reuse matrix decompositions and leverage calculations without changing the estimating equations.

  • Final dense Cholesky inference omits an unnecessary weighted-response solve, and intercept detection stops scanning a column once it is nonconstant.

  • Revised vignette explanations to define technical terms and their practical consequences, corrected outdated interface descriptions, and distinguished historical benchmark outputs from current measurements.

  • Removed sparse intercept densification and duplicate covariance inversions.

  • Reused constant-weight factors and accepted streaming weighted systems; omitted covariance calculations from mixture intermediate fits.

  • Added regression tests against base R, brglm2, and pscl, an accuracy-checked timing script, and automatic Linux/macOS/Windows package checks.

  • Expanded the vignettes and restored the static benchmark regeneration script.

fastglm 0.1.22026-08-27

Bug fixes

  • Compilation now works under libc++ with clang 23 and newer, which no longer supplies <iterator> and <algorithm> as transitive includes. The bigmemory header BigMatrix.h, pulled in by the big.matrix backend, uses std::back_inserter and std::copy without including those headers itself, so the two source files that include it (fit_glm_dense.cpp and bigmemory.cpp) now include <iterator> and <algorithm> explicitly beforehand. Reported by CRAN’s clang-trunk checks.

fastglm 0.1.12026-06-07

New features

  • Firth bias-reduced GLMs (firth = TRUE) now work for all standard families (gaussian, binomial, Poisson, Gamma, inverse.gaussian) on dense, sparse, and streaming backends. In 0.1.0 Firth was limited to binomial(link = "logit") on dense designs only.

  • SQUAREM acceleration (Varadhan and Roland, 2008) for the fastglm_zi() EM driver, converting linear EM convergence to near-quadratic.

Numerical stability

  • Negative-binomial initialization in fastglm_nb() now uses a moment-based mu/theta seed instead of always running a full pilot Poisson fit, improving convergence on overdispersed data and near boundary cases.

  • Increased the default outer.maxit for fastglm_nb() from 25 to 50 to allow convergence in harder NB problems.

  • Clamping guards in native C++ family kernels for inverse-link and sqrt-link families (Gamma, inverse.gaussian, Tweedie) to prevent overflow when eta is near zero.

  • Floor on mu.eta for Tweedie inverse and sqrt links to avoid division by zero in IRLS weights.

  • Sign correction in the Tweedie sqrt mu.eta kernel.

Bug fixes

  • Replaced Rf_error() with Rcpp::stop() in bigmemory.cpp (reported in GitHub issue).

Documentation

  • New vignette firth-fastglm covering Firth bias-reduced GLMs for all supported families.

  • New vignettes nb-convergence-fastglm and nb-stability-fastglm demonstrating fastglm_nb() convergence and stability relative to MASS::glm.nb() on challenging datasets.

  • Expanded benchmarks vignette with additional model classes.

Internal

  • Shared Brent root-finder moved to inst/include/brent.h, replacing three duplicated implementations.

  • Expanded test suite (107 test blocks / 361 expectations, up from 54 / 131 in 0.1.0), including new suites for numerical edge cases and Firth across all families.

fastglm 0.1.02026-05-05

Breaking changes

  • fastglm.fit() and fastglm.control() have been renamed to fastglm_fit() and fastglm_control(). The old dot-form names triggered an apparent-S3-method R CMD check NOTE because fastglm is itself a generic. Existing code that passes method = fastglm.fit to glm() should be updated to method = fastglm_fit.

New features

  • New top-level function fastglm_nb() for negative-binomial regression with the dispersion theta estimated jointly with the regression coefficients. Plays the same role as MASS::glm.nb(), but the IRLS loop, the inner Brent root-find for theta, and the outer (beta, theta) alternation all run entirely in C++.

  • New top-level function fastglm_hurdle() for two-part count models with a binary zero / non-zero component and a zero-truncated Poisson or NB count component. Same model as pscl::hurdle(); the joint fit runs in a single C++ driver that calls the existing IRLS solver twice and runs an inner Brent MLE for theta in the unknown-theta NB case.

  • New top-level function fastglm_zi() for zero-inflated Poisson and NB regression. Same model as pscl::zeroinfl(); the entire EM driver runs in C++, including closed-form posterior responsibilities, weighted IRLS for both M-steps, the inner Brent MLE for theta, and the analytical observed-information vcov.

  • New firth = TRUE argument to fastglm() and fastglm_fit() for Firth’s bias-reducing penalty on the score. Currently supported for family = binomial(link = "logit") on dense designs; converges in finite steps under separation, where unpenalized IRLS would diverge. Coefficients agree with logistf::logistf() to 1e-7 on the standard Heinze-Schemper test cases.

  • New built-in negbin(theta, link) family for negative-binomial regression with known dispersion, dispatched to a native C++ kernel on the log, sqrt, and identity links. Drop-in for MASS::negative.binomial(theta, link) without a hard dependency on MASS.

  • Native fast paths for the family$family == "Negative Binomial(K)" form produced by MASS::negative.binomial(), the quasibinomial() / quasipoisson() families, and statmod::tweedie(). Detection is automatic.

Documentation

  • New vignette count-firth-fastglm covering fastglm_nb(), fastglm_hurdle(), fastglm_zi(), and the firth = TRUE flag, with small inline accuracy and timing comparisons against MASS::glm.nb, pscl::hurdle, pscl::zeroinfl, and logistf::logistf.

  • New vignette benchmarks-fastglm providing a more comprehensive benchmark study at larger sample sizes, covering all six model classes. Pre-compiled at maintainer build time so it does not run during R CMD check / R CMD build and adds essentially zero time to the package check budget.

  • fastglm-overview updated with a short section introducing the new count-data and Firth entry points.

Other new features

  • Real vcov() for "fastglm" objects: the unscaled covariance is now computed in C++ from the IRLS factorisation directly and exposed as $cov.unscaled. summary.fastglm(), vcov.fastglm(), and predict.fastglm(se.fit = TRUE) now all work without a refit hack; vcov.fastglmFit() no longer re-runs glm.fit to recover a qr slot.

  • S3 methods registered on sandwich::vcovHC() and sandwich::vcovCL() for heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC0–HC3) and cluster-robust covariance matrices. After library(sandwich), vcovHC(fit) and vcovCL(fit, ...) match sandwich::vcovHC.glm() / sandwich::vcovCL.glm() to floating-point precision and work for sparse, big.matrix, and in-memory fits. (Earlier development versions shipped local vcovHC() / vcovCL() generics; those have been removed in favor of registering on the canonical sandwich generics.)

  • Sparse design matrices (Matrix::dgCMatrix) are now supported directly by fastglm() and fastglm_fit() for the LLT (method = 2) and LDLT (method = 3) Cholesky paths. Other decompositions are rejected with an informative error rather than silently densified.

  • bigmemory::big.matrix inputs now stream the design matrix in row-blocks of FASTGLM_CHUNK_ROWS rows (default 16384, user-configurable via the environment variable). Filebacked big.matrix objects no longer have to be materialised in RAM.

  • New top-level function fastglm_streaming(chunk_callback, n_chunks, family, ...) for fitting GLMs on data sources that do not fit in memory: Arrow datasets, Parquet files, DuckDB queries, CSV streamers, and any other chunk-yielding iterator. The IRLS loop, step-halving, and Cholesky solve all run in C++; the closure is invoked only to deliver one row-block at a time.

Speed

  • For standard families (gaussian / binomial / poisson / Gamma / inverse.gaussian on their common links) the per-iteration calls to family$variance, mu.eta, linkinv, and dev.resids are now evaluated in inline C++ rather than via R callbacks. Detection is automatic; non-standard families fall back to the previous R-callback path with no user-facing change.

  • The IRLS solver pre-allocates its working buffers across iterations and uses noalias() writes throughout solve_wls(). Eigen’s parallelism is no longer disabled.

  • On large n the combined effect is roughly a 1.5×–2× speed-up over fastglm 0.0.4 on the same hardware, on top of the existing 3×–10× advantage over stats::glm().

Documentation

  • New vignette fastglm-overview providing a single high-level entry point covering all of the package’s functionality.

  • New vignette large-data-fastglm walking through the three large-data paths (sparse, big.matrix, streaming callback) end to end, including the Arrow / Parquet recipe.

Internal

  • New tests/testthat/ suite covering vcov(), native vs callback family dispatch, sparse fits, big.matrix streaming, callback-based streaming, and robust SE.

fastglm 0.0.4 and earlier2025-12-16

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.

  • Added fastglm.fit() to be used as a fitting method for glm().

  • Documentation and vignette updates.
